prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” roofer for every Dallas roof replacement — the right company depends on your location, roof size/type, budget, warranty needs, whether you’re using insurance, and how quickly you need the work done. I can find and recommend specific, well‑vetted contractors for your job if you tell me your ZIP code and a few details (roof size or square footage, shingle vs. metal, insurance claim?).

If you want help now, here’s what I recommend and how to pick the best one for your project.

What to tell me so I can give tailored recommendations
- Your ZIP code or neighborhood in Dallas
- Approximate roof size or house square footage
- Roof type (asphalt shingles, metal, flat/low slope, tile)
- Are you filing an insurance claim?
- Desired timeline and budget range
- Any must‑have certifications or warranty needs

How to evaluate and choose the best Dallas roofer
1. Credentials and insurance
   - Verify general liability insurance and workers’ compensation (ask for certificates).
   - Confirm they’re registered to do business in Texas (and ask if they pull permits).
   - Look for manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) if you want extended warranties.

2. Reputation and reviews
   - Check Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, and the BBB.
   - Ask for local references and photos of recent Dallas-area jobs.

3. Written estimates and scope
   - Get at least 2–3 written estimates with the same scope (materials, tear‑off vs overlay, underlayment, flashing, ventilation).
   - Make sure the contract lists start/finish dates, payment schedule, cleanup, and the warranty terms.

4. Warranties
   - Distinguish manufacturer (shingle) warranty from contractor workmanship warranty; get both in writing.
   - Ask about the process for warranty claims and who services them.

5. Insurance claim experience (if applicable)
   - If you’re using homeowner’s insurance, ask if they help document damage, provide a roof inspection report, and work with adjusters (but beware contractors who direct you to accept the insurer’s first offer without review).

6. Red flags
   - High-pressure sales tactics, “storm-chaser” crews who canvass neighborhoods after storms.
   - Requests for large upfront cash payments or “sign today for a discount.”
   - No physical address or poor communication.

Questions to ask each roofer
- Are you licensed/registered in Texas and insured? Can you provide certificates?
- Are you a certified installer for the brand of shingle I want?
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?
- What is included in the price (decking repair, flashing, drip edge, underlayment, ventilation)?
- What warranties do I get (manufacturer + workmanship), and are they transferable?
- What is your cleanup process and will you use a magnet to pick up nails?
- Can you provide references from jobs in my neighborhood?

If you want, I can:
- Pull a short list (3–5) of top-rated roofers in your Dallas ZIP with links to reviews and contact info.
- Review 2–3 estimates you receive and help compare them line‑by‑line.
Tell me your ZIP code and any other details and I’ll find the best local options.
